reading.title: From manuscripts to subscriptions
reading.text: Before the printing press, every book was a manuscript, copied by hand over many months. Historians describe monasteries as the libraries of medieval Europe, and inscriptions on stone were often the only public texts. Today, the situation is reversed: text is everywhere and almost free. Readers subscribe to newsletters, students download transcripts of lectures, and doctors send prescriptions by email. Some writers worry that we read more but think less. Others reply that more people can now write and publish than at any time in history.
